$schema: DevNotes log — deviations, discoveries, decisions captured during build

notes.content: Image payload format: plan specified `{ type: 'image', source: { type: 'base64', mediaType: 'image/png', data } }` (anthropic SDK shape) but the canonical pi-coding-agent ImageContent shape (per node_modules/.../docs/rpc.md and what CP1's orchestrator.ts uses) is `{ type: 'image', data, mimeType: 'image/png' }`. Used the latter to match CP1 and the typed PromptOptions.images: ImageContent[].

Plan action 11 said pass `tools: createCodingTools(input.resolved.assetDir)` to createAgentSession. CreateAgentSessionOptions.tools is typed as `string[]` (an allowlist of tool names), not `Tool[]`. Omitted the tools param entirely — matches CP1's working pattern where the default coding tools are auto-enabled and resolve paths against the explicit `cwd: resolved.assetDir`.
Truncated rawFirst/rawSecond to 400 chars before stuffing into the parse_failed CritiqueOutcome variant (per the read-before note recommending reuse of the existing truncate helper).

Used `.ts` module specifiers in src/tui.ts imports (./critic.ts, ./usage.ts) rather than the plan's `.js` specifiers, to match the existing convention in src/orchestrator.ts, src/fixStep.ts, etc. tsconfig has allowImportingTsExtensions=true and noEmit=true so this is well-supported.

Added a private issuesBox Box field on AssetLoopTUI rather than reaching into this.tui.children[4] by index — functionally equivalent to the plan's swap-via-index approach but less brittle if panel ordering ever changes. setIssues/setCurrentIssue mutate this.issuesList and re-home it via issuesBox.clear()+addChild(this.issuesList), exactly as the plan prescribed.

Plan action 6 called for inserting `const renderBase64 = readFileSync(resolved.renderPath).toString("base64"); tui.setRender(...); tui.setPhase("critique");` after renderWithPlaywright. Orchestrator already declared renderBase64 at that exact spot (from CP1/CP2/CP3), so redeclaring would be a TS2451 error. Reused the existing renderBase64 and inserted only `tui.setRender(renderBase64, "image/png"); tui.setPhase("critique");` after it.

Left the legacy `console.log("phase: ...")` and `console.log("fix I1: ...")` and `console.log("accepted — ...")` lines in place this checkpoint — plan did not call for their removal and they still produce useful logs when the TUI is not attached to a TTY. They may visually interfere with the pi-tui differential render in a live terminal; CP5 `cleanup, summary, end-to-end validation` is the natural place to purge or gate them.

try/finally wraps the remainder of runAssetLoop after `process.once('SIGINT', sigintHandler)`. The body is intentionally left at its original indent (one level shallow of the new try{}) to minimize diff churn; finally only unregisters the SIGINT listener and deliberately does not call tui.stop() — the three terminal branches (hit_empty, cap, parse-failure) plus the SIGINT handler itself already handle teardown, and pi-tui TUI.stop is idempotent per its `stopped` flag.

Verification step 'Manual end-to-end in a Kitty/Ghostty/iTerm2/WezTerm terminal' cannot be performed in background build mode — no interactive terminal, no credentials vetted for a fresh asset dir, no network egress guarantees. Typecheck (npm run typecheck) passes cleanly, which is the only automated gate available. Manual TUI validation is deferred to the human operator (same pattern as CP1–CP3).

Plan action 9 prescribed `lines.push(\`usage: ${formatUsageSnapshot(input.usage)}\`)` but formatUsageSnapshot already returns a string starting with the literal `usage: ` prefix (apps/pi-asset-loop/src/usage.ts:80). Following the plan literally would yield a doubled prefix `usage: usage: calls=...`, which contradicts the CP5 verification (TG3 T5 action 4) that expects a single `usage: calls=...` line. Pushed `formatUsageSnapshot(input.usage)` directly so the helper emits one canonical usage line.

After deleting extensions/asset-loop.ts, the verification check `rg 'extensions/asset-loop' apps/pi-asset-loop` (TG3 T5 action 6) still matched apps/pi-asset-loop/README.md line 19, which documented the legacy `pi -e ./extensions/asset-loop.ts` invocation. Made a minimal edit to the Run section (now `cd apps/pi-asset-loop && bun run asset-loop --asset ../../runs/<run>/assets/<id>`) so the cleanliness assertion passes. The rest of README.md is broadly stale (still calls the project a 'Pi coding-agent extension', references a 10-iteration cap instead of 15, and describes the old accepted.json `{score, notes}` shape) — left for the docs phase to rewrite holistically rather than a piecemeal patch in build.

TG3 T5 runtime verification (actions 2–5: pick a fresh asset dir, `bun run asset-loop` end-to-end in a Kitty/Ghostty/iTerm2/WezTerm terminal, eyeball the post-stop summary block in scrollback, `jq 'keys | sort' accepted.json` for the 8-key shape) cannot run in background build mode — needs an interactive terminal for the pi-tui Image components, vetted Anthropic credentials, and the operator's consent to spend real LLM dollars on a 1–15 iteration loop. The four static assertions ran cleanly: (1) `npm run typecheck` exit 0, (6) `rg 'extensions/asset-loop' apps/pi-asset-loop` zero matches after the README minor edit, (7) `test ! -d apps/pi-asset-loop/extensions` exit 0, (8) `jq '.scripts | keys | sort' apps/pi-asset-loop/package.json` exactly `["asset-loop","postinstall","typecheck"]`. Marking CP5 complete on the static gates with the runtime verification deferred to the operator (same pattern as CP1–CP4).
